title: Open a new superglue tube: unscrew the cap, flip it and pierce the foil seal with its pin
instruction: Unscrew the glue tube's cap, flip it over, and use the pin on top of the cap to pierce the foil seal on the nozzle without squeezing the tube. Leave the cap and tube released.
context: Opening a new tube of superglue is a familiar household moment: the nozzle is sealed with foil and the cap carries a pin for breaking it. You unscrew the cap, turn it upside down, and push the pin squarely into the nozzle. Squeezing the soft tube while doing it squirts glue onto your fingers and the bench. The task combines a real thread turn, reorienting a small part in the hand, and a square, centred push that must not crush the soft body beside it.
setup: A glue-style tube stands nozzle-up in a 70 x 50 x 20 mm rigid bench holder at the bench centre. Simulator: soft 42 x 14 x 80 mm body, 20 mm shoulder, 14 mm neck (1.5 mm pitch), 2.5 mm radius nozzle sealed by a 9 mm foil disc that tears at about 3 N; red 18 x 22 mm, 8 g cap screwed on, its 3 mm pin pointing up. Real station: one fresh, unopened empty aluminium squeeze tube with a blind (membrane-sealed) nozzle and its own piercing-pin cap (sold as 'empty aluminium toothpaste/paint tubes with needle cap'), filled through the open tail with plain petroleum jelly and fold-sealed; no glue is used. Reference marks: a paint line across cap and shoulder, a paint ring on the pin 2 mm from its tip, and a 1 mm grid card behind the nozzle seen by two fixed phone cameras (front and side). Tube and holder are fixed. Nothing else is on the bench.
scoring: 0.25 once the cap has been turned 1.5 turns counter-clockwise and lifted 25 mm from its seat; 0.5 once it is also upside down (pin within 5 degrees of straight down) with the pin tip within 1.5 mm of the nozzle axis; 0.75 once the tip is 2 mm past the seal face, aligned, and the seal has broken; 1.0 once the tip has also been withdrawn 30 mm, both gripper centre points (TCPs) are at least 4 cm from the cap and nozzle, and all is still for 1 s. Any gripper touching within 5 mm of the soft body, a pin driven at more than 10 degrees tilt, the seal breached without the pin, or the cap dropped off the bench scores 0 for the episode. Real trial: turns are counted from the paint line in the video; lift, 1.5 mm offset, tilt, withdrawal and clearance are read in the two camera views against the 1 mm grid card; 2 mm penetration counts when the pin's 2 mm paint ring reaches the nozzle lip in the side view and a post-trial loupe photo shows a hole in the membrane inside the nozzle bore. Squeezing counts as any gripper contact with the tube body in either view or a new dent in the aluminium body in before/after photos.
reset_notes: Remove the used tube. Fresh seal (about 3 min, or batch-prepared): take a new unopened needle-cap tube, check the nozzle membrane is intact, fill it from the open tail with 10 ml petroleum jelly from a syringe, fold the tail three times with flat pliers, screw its cap fully on and paint the cap/shoulder line and the 2 mm pin ring. Seat it in the holder. Wipe the gripper pads with a dry paper towel; the jelly is non-curing and inert.
fidelity: Rigid-body Isaac Sim/PhysX, 20 Hz. The soft body is a rigid block; squeezing is a 5 mm proximity check, not force. The thread is a spring slide released after 1.5 turns. The seal is a disc on a 3 N break joint; the bore is not modelled, so cap and foil pass through the nozzle. Real tube body, cap and thread sizes and membrane tear force differ and are unmeasured. No fill or glue is simulated.
